summary: DAY red-team independently challenged every company in the 12-name Chief batch. The dominant shared failure mode is not weak headline demand; it is concentration and execution fragility hidden underneath exceptionally strong AI/space infrastructure growth. No bearish conclusion is forced. Every company remains open because at least one material falsification question lacks filing-level closure.

companies.redTeamCase: Vertical integration and M&A can widen capability faster than internal controls/cash conversion mature; Neutron is a high-value schedule and capital-risk node.
contradictions: record backlog and contracts versus still-unproven Neutron flight qualification and integration burden
unknowns: normalized post-M&A cash burn, acquisition accounting and dilution
companies.falsifier: successful Neutron qualification plus sustained backlog conversion without material financing dependence would weaken the bear case

companies.redTeamCase: Explosive growth can mask hyperscaler concentration and design-cycle dependence; customer insourcing or alternative interconnect architectures could compress both growth and valuation simultaneously.
unknowns: true end-customer concentration, acquisition cash bridge and current program duration
companies.falsifier: broader named-customer diversification and multi-generation design wins would materially weaken concentration risk

companies.redTeamCase: Scorpio becoming the largest family ahead of plan increases product-ramp concentration even as total portfolio broadens. Warrant/control mechanics can create asymmetric dilution/governance risk in a high-expectation name.
contradictions: management describes diversified growth while exact end-customer concentration remains unresolved
unknowns: customer mapping, control ownership and future warrant vesting
companies.falsifier: revenue diversification across multiple end customers and product lines with stable dilution would weaken this case

companies.redTeamCase: Scale leadership can obscure policy and buyer concentration. Export controls can strand inventory/addressable demand while hyperscalers increasingly pursue custom silicon and bargaining leverage.
unknowns: indirect hyperscaler concentration and normalized capital-return/dilution bridge
companies.falsifier: continued broad customer diversification and sustained economics despite tighter export controls/custom silicon would weaken the threat

companies.redTeamCase: Large announced deployments may not equal durable accelerator share; AMD must prove software/platform stickiness and economics rather than relying on second-source demand during an AI capex boom.
contradictions: record data-center growth is strong evidence of demand but not sufficient evidence of durable share
unknowns: MI-series unit economics, customer concentration and long-run ROCm switching costs
companies.falsifier: repeat multi-generation deployments with rising gross profit and software adoption would weaken the bear case

companies.redTeamCase: Custom AI silicon growth can be exceptionally profitable but concentrated in a few programs/customers. VMware-era debt and tax indemnity/refinancing tails reduce margin for error if AI growth disappoints.
unknowns: current AI customer concentration and exact refinancing/tax tail sensitivity
companies.falsifier: customer diversification plus continued deleveraging despite lower AI growth would weaken this case

companies.redTeamCase: Best-in-class margins can coexist with geopolitical single-point-of-failure risk and expensive overseas redundancy. AI/customer concentration may amplify cyclicality at peak utilization.
unknowns: latest customer concentration and overseas-fab normalized returns
companies.falsifier: successful overseas ramp with structurally strong returns and broader customer mix would weaken the risk

companies.redTeamCase: Monopoly-like lithography power creates regulatory/export and supplier single-point sensitivity. A handful of irreplaceable suppliers or geopolitical restrictions can turn backlog into delayed revenue despite demand.
unknowns: quantified critical supplier concentration and China/export exposure
companies.falsifier: demonstrated supplier redundancy and sustained shipments through tighter controls would weaken the case

companies.redTeamCase: Entering production silicon may expand TAM but risks channel conflict with licensees. SoftBank control and related-party economics can weaken minority-holder governance clarity.
contradictions: platform neutrality is strategically valuable while direct silicon competes closer to customers/licensees
unknowns: SoftBank/control economics, related-party terms, customer concentration and AGI CPU margins
companies.falsifier: licensee ecosystem remains broad and growing while direct silicon produces incremental economics without churn

companies.redTeamCase: HBM scarcity can drive peak economics just before capacity catches up. Memory remains cyclical and capital intensive; current strength must survive a supply response.
unknowns: fresh capex/debt normalization and HBM supply-demand duration
companies.falsifier: multi-year HBM pricing/margin resilience despite large industry capex would weaken the cycle-peak case

companies.redTeamCase: Ethernet AI growth can be real while hyperscalers still internalize networking or use white-box/custom systems. Large-customer concentration can hide behind aggregate growth.
unknowns: latest filing-level large-customer percentages and custom-network displacement rate
companies.falsifier: share gains across diversified AI customers while gross margin remains resilient would weaken substitution risk

companies.redTeamCase: A 2.9x book-to-bill and giant backlog can signal scarcity, but also creates schedule/cancellation risk if hyperscaler plans move. Advanced payments may flatter near-term cash conversion relative to ultimate project economics.
contradictions: investment-grade refinancing lowers balance-sheet risk while backlog concentration/cancellation risk rises with scale
unknowns: latest customer concentration, backlog cancellation/reschedule terms and advanced-payment contribution to cash flow
companies.falsifier: sustained backlog conversion, low cancellations and diversified customer growth would weaken the case

contradictions: Strong AI demand across the batch does not resolve whether returns are durable after customer concentration, export controls, supply response and vertical integration are normalized.
Backlog/order growth at RKLB and VRT is supportive but must not be treated as cash-like without cancellation/conversion evidence.
Company-reported customer diversification claims at ALAB/others are not equivalent to filing-level end-customer concentration disclosure.
unknowns: No batch member has a fully closed current-cycle concentration and substitution test.
Market-wide AI capex normalization timing remains unknown and is a correlated risk across NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSM, ASML, MU, ANET, ALAB, CRDO and VRT.
Exact post-M&A integration/capital structure normalization remains incomplete for RKLB and some acquisition-heavy peers.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting: prioritize filing-level concentration/customer disclosures for CRDO, ALAB, NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSM and ANET.
Structural-causal: test whether custom silicon/white-box networking is a successor bottleneck migration rather than simple substitution.
Expectations-execution: penalize correlated AI-capex exposure until current valuation/consensus data can distinguish great company from priced-for-perfection security.
blockingIssues: filing-level customer concentration incomplete across multiple batch names
cycle-normalized capex and dilution evidence incomplete for RKLB, MU and other capital-intensive names
export-control scenario sensitivity remains unresolved for NVDA, AMD, ASML and indirectly TSM
